stanzas: אֲדוֹן עוֹלָם אֲשֶׁר מָלַךְ – בְּטֶרֶם כָּל־יְצִיר נִבְרָא,
לְעֵת נַעְשָׂה בְחֶפְצוֹ כֹּל – אֲזַי מֶלֶךְ שְׁמוֹ נִקְרָא,
וְאַחֲרֵי כִּכְלוֹת הַכֹּל – לְבַדּוֹ יִמְלוֹךְ נוֹרָא,
וְהוּא הָיָה, וְהוּא הוֹוֶה, וְהוּא יִהְיֶה – בְּתִפְאָרָה.
וְהוּא אֶחָד, וְאֵין שֵׁנִי לְהַמְשִׁילוֹ וּלְהַחְבִּירָה –
בְּלִי רֵאשִׁית, בְּלִי תַכְלִית, וְלוֹ הָעוֹז וְהַמִּשְׂרָה,
[בְּלִי עֵרֶךְ, בְּלִי דִמְיוֹן, בְּלִי שִׁנּוּי וּתְמוּרָה,
בְּלִי חִבּוּר, בְּלִי פֵרוּד, גְּדוֹל כּוֹחַ וּגְבוּרָה.]
וְהוּא אֵלִי וְחַי גּוֹאֲלִי, וְצוּר־חֶבְלִי בְּ[יוֹם]־צָרָה,
וְהוּא נִסִּי וּמְנוּסִי – מְנַת כּוֹסִי בְּיוֹם אֶקְרָא,
[וְהוּא רוֹפֵא, וְהוּא מַרְפֵּא, וְהוּא צוֹפֶה, וְהוּא עֶזְרָה.]
בְּיָדוֹ אַפְקִיד רוּחִי בְּעֵת אִישַׁן וְאָעִירָה,
וְעִם רוּחִי, גְּוִיָּתִי – יְיָ לִי וְלֹא אִירָא.
[בְּמִקְדָּשׁוֹ תָּגֵל נַפְשִׁי, מְשִׁיחֵנוּ יִשְלַח מְהֵרָה,
וְאָז נָשִׁיר בְּבֵית קָדְּשִׁי, אָמֵן, אָמֵן! שֵם הַנּוֹרָא:]
Lord of the world, who reigned – before any form was created,
at the time when all was made by his will – then his name was called King,
and after all has come to an end – he alone will reign, awesome,
and he was, and he is, and he will be – in splendour.
And he is one, and there is no second to liken to him or to set beside him –
without beginning, without end, and his are the strength and the dominion,
[without measure, without likeness, without change or exchange,
without joining, without parting, great in strength and might.]
And he is my God, and my redeemer lives, and the rock of my pangs [?] in the [day](time) of trouble,
and he is my banner and my refuge – the portion of my cup on the day I call,
[and he is healer, and he is healing, and he watches, and he is help.]
Into his hand I entrust my spirit, when I sleep and I wake,
and with my spirit, my body – the Lord is with me, and I shall not fear.
[In his sanctuary my soul will rejoice; may he send our anointed one soon,
and then we shall sing in my holy house, Amen, amen! the awesome name:]
adon 'olam asher malakh – beterem kol-yetsir nivra,
le'et na'asah vekheftso kol – azai melekh shemo nikra,
ve'akharei kikhlot hakkol – levaddo yimlokh nora,
vehu hayah, vehu hoveh, vehu yihyeh – betif'arah.
vehu ekhad, ve'ein sheni lehamshilo ulehakhbirah –
beli reshit, beli takhlit, velo ha'oz vehammisrah,
[beli 'erekh, beli dimyon, beli shinnui utemurah,
beli khibbur, beli ferud, gedol koakh ugevurah.]
vehu eli vekhai go'ali, vetsur-khevli be[yom]('et)-tsarah,
vehu nissi umenusi – menat kosi beyom ekra,
[vehu rofe, vehu marpe, vehu tsofeh, vehu 'ezrah.]
beyado afkid rukhi be'et ishan ve'a'irah,
ve'im rukhi, geviyyati – Adonai li velo ira.
[bemikdasho tagel nafshi, meshikhenu yishlakh meherah,
ve'az nashir beveit kodshi, amen, amen! shem hannora:]

notes: The Wikisource text carries editorial source references in parentheses inside the lines (Isaiah 45:7 and the Yotser Or blessing, 1 Kings 9:11, Tractate Soferim 14:4, Ecclesiastes 4:8, Psalm 31:6, Psalm 118:6). They are not part of the hymn and are left out of en and rom; the editor may want them stripped from orig as well, or shown as notes.
Lines in square brackets (7-8, 11, 14-15) are the Wikisource edition's marking of lines not sung in every rite; the brackets are kept in en and rom.
line 1.9: 'be[yom](et)' is the edition's variant notation: 'on the day of trouble', with 'in the time of trouble' as the other reading. Kept as written.
line 1.9: 'tsur chevli' is disputed: chevel can mean pangs or travail (as rendered, hence [?]) or a lot, portion (the rock of my portion).
line 1.5: 'ulehachbirah', literally 'to make (it) a companion', with a feminine ending for the rhyme; rendered 'to set beside him'.
line 1.13: yod-yod (YY) is the liturgical abbreviation for the divine name, read Adonai; romanized as Adonai.
Romanization: initial aleph unmarked, other aleph and all ayin as '; dagesh forte doubled except in the digraphs sh, ts, kh; maqqef as a hyphen.
